# Contigs-based analysis of KEGG genes


# 1. Load KEGG data


```{r}
library('phyloseq')
library("cowplot")
library("dplyr")
library("ggplot2")
library("vegan")
library("microbiome")
library("tibble")
library("readxl")
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

setwd('C:\\Users\\lehakkin\\RStudio_computer')

# load the coverage data
load(file = 'KOfam_metabolism_ps_COVERAGE_FINAL_PNSCO2')
ps

meta <- meta(ps)

ps_RA <- transform(ps, "compositional")
```






# 2. PCoA for KEGG composition



To visualize beta diversity, I will do a PCoA which is metric instead of e.g. non-metric NMDS

I will be following somewhat this tutorial:

[Joey Bernhardt](https://github.com/JoeyBernhardt/NumericalEcology/blob/master/Num._Ecology_Chap._9.md)




```{r}
OTU = as(otu_table(ps_RA), "matrix")
# transpose if necessary
if(taxa_are_rows(ps_RA)){OTU <- t(OTU)}
# Coerce to data.frame
OTU = as.data.frame(OTU)
OTU <- as.matrix(OTU)

bray_dist <- vegan::vegdist(OTU, method="bray")
str(bray_dist)

# use k = 3 so we'll get calculations for three axes
pcoa <- cmdscale(bray_dist, eig=TRUE, k = 3)
ordiplot(scores(pcoa),display="sites", type="points")
```


Let's first make PCoA ordination with axes 1 and 2, and later for 1 and 3.

Env. variables

```{r}
# Post-Hoc Projections of environmental variables
# envfit in vegan projects points onto vectors that have maximum correlation with corresponding environmental variables
pcoa.env12 <- envfit(pcoa, meta[ ,c("pH_H2O", "EC_uScm", "C_g_per_kg", "N_gkg", "TP_gkg", "sample_type", "depth_numerical", "DOC_mgkg", "Pinorg_mgkg", "Porg_mgkg", "log_root", "C_per_N", "Feox_mmolkg", "Alox_mmolkg", "oxides_mmolkg", "PH2O_mgkg")], na.rm = TRUE, choices=c(1:2), permutations = 999)

    

# main effects
pcoa.env12

ef12.adj <- pcoa.env12
pvals.adj <- p.adjust (pcoa.env12$vectors$pvals, method = 'bonferroni')
ef12.adj$vectors$pvals <- pvals.adj
ef12.adj

```


To plot (classical) mds (which is equivalent to PCoA) with ggplot a new datasheet needs to be created which contains the x,y points for each site. You can do this by calling the scores of you mds.




```{r}
site.scrs <- as.data.frame(scores(pcoa, display = "sites")) #save pcoa results into dataframe
site.scrs <- cbind(site.scrs, soil_type = meta$sample_type) #add grouping variable "soil_type" to dataframe
site.scrs <- cbind(site.scrs, depth = meta$depth) #add grouping variable of depth

head(site.scrs)
```


Categorial and continuous variables

```{r}

# first categorial variables
env.scores_cat12 <- as.data.frame(scores(pcoa.env12, display = "factors"))*0.25 # multiply the envfit scores to keep them in the frame of the ordination
env.scores_cat12 <- cbind(env.scores_cat12, env.variables = rownames(env.scores_cat12)) #and then gives them their names

env.scores_cat12 <- cbind(env.scores_cat12, pval = pcoa.env12$factors$pvals) # add pvalues to dataframe
sig.env.scores_cat12 <- subset(env.scores_cat12, pval<=0.05) #subset data to show variables significant at 0.05
sig.env.scores_cat12
# all were significant


# then continous variables
env.scores_cont12 <- as.data.frame(scores(pcoa.env12, display = "vectors"))*0.25 # multiply the envfit scores to keep them in the frame of the ordination
env.scores_cont12 <- cbind(env.scores_cont12, env.variables = rownames(env.scores_cont12)) #and then gives them their names

env.scores_cont12 <- cbind(env.scores_cont12, pval = pcoa.env12$vectors$pvals) # add pvalues to dataframe
sig.env.scores_cont12 <- subset(env.scores_cont12, pval<=0.05) #subset data to show variables significant at 0.05
sig.env.scores_cont12
# all were significant
```



Now we have the relevant information for plotting the ordination in ggplot


```{r}
MyPalette <- c(forest = "#1167b1", meadow = "#fbc02d", organic = "#8a8a8a", conventional =  "#b71c1c")

site.scrs$new_depth <- site.scrs$depth

site.scrs$new_depth <- gsub("...", "-", site.scrs$new_depth, fixed = TRUE)
```

# 3. PERMANOVA of KEGG genes


No forest

```{r}
# subset samples
ps_RA <- subset_samples(ps_RA, sample_type != "forest")
meta_subset <- meta(ps_RA)


# You have only submitted samples, not OTUs. Define prevalence of each taxa
# (in how many samples did each taxa appear at least once)
prev0 = apply(X = otu_table(ps_RA),
              MARGIN = ifelse(taxa_are_rows(ps_RA), yes = 1, no = 2),
              FUN = function(x){sum(x > 0)})

# Execute prevalence filter, using `prune_taxa()` function
ps_RA = prune_taxa((prev0 > 0), ps_RA)
ps_RA
```


Calculate Bray-Curtis (dis)similarities

```{r}
ps_RA_bray <- phyloseq::distance(ps_RA, method = "bray")
```


Homogenity of variances

Check that variance homogeneity assumptions hold (to ensure the reliability of the results). If  groups have signif. different spreads the permanova result may be potentially explained by that, rtaher than the groups.

Betadisper first calculates the average distance of group members to the group centroid in multivariate space (generated by a distance matrix). Then, an ANOVA is done to test if the dispersions (variances) of groups are different.

for management type

```{r}
anova(betadisper(ps_RA_bray, meta$sample_type))
```
         

We see that the ANOVA p-value is NOT significant meaning that the **homogeneity of variance assumption is met**


for depth

```{r}
anova(betadisper(ps_RA_bray, meta$depth))
```

We see that the ANOVA p-value is significant meaning that **homogeneity of variance assumption is NOT met**


post hoc

I'll do post hoc analysis with Tukey's test to see which groups differ in relation to their variances

```{r}
TukeyHSD(betadisper(ps_RA_bray, meta$depth))
```

Only the soil layer 40-80 cm differs from 30-40 cm


## 3.1. Initial PERMANOVAs




```{r}
# first with just soil type and strata option
adonis2(formula = ps_RA_bray~ sample_type, data = meta, permutations = 999, method = "bray", by = "margin", strata = meta$depth)
```

Significant




Depth

```{r}
# then with just depth and strata option
adonis2(formula = ps_RA_bray~ depth, data = meta, permutations = 9999, method = "bray", by = "margin", strata = meta$sample_type)
```

Depth has a larger effect. So, let's put it first in the model


## 3.2. Final PERMANOVA

For the full model it matters which "by" option we choose. When by="terms" significance for each term is calculated sequentially from first to last, so that the order of terms matter. We will use this, because with sequential analysis we will get R2 values that sum up to 1, and will also get the significance and R2 values for each interaction term separately rather than for the interaction alone.

Note! Setting by = "terms" will assess significance for each term (sequentially from first to last), by = "margin" will assess the marginal effects of the terms (each marginal term analysed in a model with all other variables)




```{r}
set.seed(270285)
final <- adonis2(formula = ps_RA_bray ~ depth * sample_type, data = meta, permutations = 9999, method = "bray", by = "terms")
final

```





# 4. Heatmaps of KEGG

## 4.1. CO2 fixation

### 4.1.1. pathway



I will do heatmap for RA values.

For the final heatmap figure the RA values will be standardizes (z-transformed)

Note! I will not do Z-transforming the data before plotting the heatmap. Instead I will do row scaling in the Pheatmap stage, which means that each gene's relative abundance is standardized



Subset the CO2-fixing


```{r}
ps_RA <- transform(ps, "compositional")
ps_co2fix <- subset_taxa(ps_RA, metabolism == "CO2_fixing")
ps_co2fix

ps_co2fix <- aggregate_rare(ps_co2fix, level = 'pathway', detection = 0/100, prevalence = 0/140)
ps_co2fix

```



```{r}
meta <- meta(ps_co2fix)

meta$Depth <- gsub("...", "-", meta$depth, fixed = TRUE)

meta$Depth[meta$Depth=="40-"] <- "40-80"


meta$Depth[meta$Depth=="0-10"] <- "0-10 cm"
meta$Depth[meta$Depth=="10-20"] <- "10-20 cm"
meta$Depth[meta$Depth=="20-30"] <- "20-30 cm"
meta$Depth[meta$Depth=="30-40"] <- "30-40 cm"
meta$Depth[meta$Depth=="40-80"] <- "40-80 cm"

meta$sample_type <- factor(meta$sample_type, levels = c("forest", "meadow", "organic", "conventional"))

# Z-transform
#ps_co2fix_z <- microbiome::transform(ps_co2fix, 'Z', log10 = FALSE)
ps_co2fix_z <- ps_co2fix

data_subset <- as(otu_table(ps_co2fix_z), "matrix")
data_subset <- as.matrix(data_subset)

# add annotations "Depth" and "Treatment"
my_sample_col <- data.frame(meta[c("Depth", "sample_type")], row.names = row.names(meta))
colnames(my_sample_col) <- c("Depth", "Treatment")


x <- as.data.frame(t(data_subset))
y <- as.data.frame(my_sample_col)
colnames(y) <- c("Depth", "sample_type")
z <- dplyr::left_join(rownames_to_column(x), rownames_to_column(y), by=c("rowname" = "rowname"))
colnames(z)[1] <- "ID"

# make into mean per treatment and soil layer
f <- z %>%
  group_by(sample_type, Depth) %>%
  summarise_all(mean)

# remove ID column
f <- f[ , -3]

# make new ID column, which is the soiltypedepth
library(stringr)
f$ID <- str_c(f$sample_type, '_', f$Depth)

# make new df with just sample type, depth and sampletypedepth
df <- f[c("sample_type", "Depth", "ID")]
# remove extra columns from f
f2 <- f[, -c(1, 2, 7)]
# column into rownames
rownames(f2) <- f$ID
# make into numeric matrix
f3 <- data.matrix(f2, rownames.force = NA)
f4 <- t(f3)

# same for df
# remove extra columns from df
df2 <- df[ , -c(3)]
# column into rownames
rownames(df2) <- df$ID
my_sample_col2 <- df2
my_sample_col3 <- as.data.frame(my_sample_col2)
rownames(my_sample_col3) <- df$ID
# lets add annotations of samples

# add annotations "Depth" and "soil_type" and change order
colnames(my_sample_col3) <- c("Treatment", "Depth")
my_sample_col3 <- my_sample_col3[, c(2,1)]

```





```{r}
# 1. Prepare group data
group <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps))
group <- subset(group, metabolism=="CO2_fixing")
group <- group[!duplicated(group[c('pathway')]), ]
rownames(group) <- group$pathway  # Ensure pathway names are row names
group <- group[match(rownames(f4), rownames(group)), ]  # Match order with f4

# Clean pathway names (no annotation needed)
group$pathway <- factor(group$pathway)  # Ensure it's a factor

# Order f4 rows by pathway (no gaps needed if no annotation)
f4_ordered <- f4[order(group$pathway), ]

row_gaps <- cumsum(table(group$pathway))[-length(table(group$pathway))]



#Create color palette
my_colour = list(
  "Treatment" = c(forest = "#1167b1", meadow = "#fbc02d", organic = "#8a8a8a", conventional =  "#b71c1c"),
  Depth = c('0-10 cm' = "#387212", '10-20 cm' = "#ADC476", '20-30 cm' = "#D8D2BA",'30-40 cm' = "#907852", '40-80 cm' = "#6A4C3A"))

# add gap between sample_types
gp_col = which(diff(as.numeric(factor(my_sample_col3$Treatment)))!=0)
```


```{r}
row.names(f4_ordered)
```


```{r}
# Change pathway names and remove unwanted

## these will be removed: C4_Dicarboxylic_acid_cycle
# row of data frame


row.names(f4_ordered)[1] <- "Arnon-Buchanan cycle"  
row.names(f4_ordered)[2] <- "Calvin cycle"
row.names(f4_ordered)[3] <- "Hydroxypropionate bicycle"  
row.names(f4_ordered)[4] <- "Wood-Ljungdahl pathway" 
```




```{r}
library("ggplotify")
library("pheatmap")
p2 <- as.ggplot(function() pheatmap(f4_ordered, cluster_cols = FALSE, cluster_rows = TRUE, annotation_col = my_sample_col3, annotation_colors = my_colour, gaps_col = gp_col, color=colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "red"))(50), show_colnames = FALSE, legend = TRUE, border_color = NA, cellheight = 16, fontsize = 14, fontsize_row = 14, annotation_names_row = FALSE, gaps_row = row_gaps, annotation_names_col = FALSE, scale = "row"))

p2
```

## 4.2. P-cycling


### 4.2.1. pathway

```{r}
ps_RA <- transform(ps, "compositional")

ps_x <- subset_taxa(ps_RA, metabolism=="P_cycling")
ps_x

x <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_x))
x <- x[, c(6, 1:5)]

tax_table(ps_x) <- tax_table(as.matrix(x))

ps_p <- aggregate_rare(ps_x, level = 'pathway', detection = 0/100, prevalence = 0/140)
ps_p
```


```{r}
meta <- meta(ps_p)

meta$Depth <- gsub("...", "-", meta$depth, fixed = TRUE)

meta$Depth[meta$Depth=="40-"] <- "40-80"


meta$Depth[meta$Depth=="0-10"] <- "0-10 cm"
meta$Depth[meta$Depth=="10-20"] <- "10-20 cm"
meta$Depth[meta$Depth=="20-30"] <- "20-30 cm"
meta$Depth[meta$Depth=="30-40"] <- "30-40 cm"
meta$Depth[meta$Depth=="40-80"] <- "40-80 cm"

meta$sample_type <- factor(meta$sample_type, levels = c("forest", "meadow", "organic", "conventional"))

# Z-transform
#ps_p_z <- microbiome::transform(ps_p, 'Z', log10 = FALSE)
ps_p_z <- ps_p

data_subset <- as(otu_table(ps_p_z), "matrix")
data_subset <- as.matrix(data_subset)

# add annotations "Depth" and "Treatment"
my_sample_col <- data.frame(meta[c("Depth", "sample_type")], row.names = row.names(meta))
colnames(my_sample_col) <- c("Depth", "Treatment")


x <- as.data.frame(t(data_subset))
y <- as.data.frame(my_sample_col)
colnames(y) <- c("Depth", "sample_type")
z <- dplyr::left_join(rownames_to_column(x), rownames_to_column(y), by=c("rowname" = "rowname"))
colnames(z)[1] <- "ID"

# make into mean per treatment and soil layer
f <- z %>%
  group_by(sample_type, Depth) %>%
  summarise_all(mean)

# remove ID column
f <- f[ , -3]

# make new ID column, which is the soiltypedepth
library(stringr)
f$ID <- str_c(f$sample_type, '_', f$Depth)

# make new df with just sample type, depth and sampletypedepth
df <- f[c("sample_type", "Depth", "ID")]
# remove extra columns from f
f2 <- f[, -c(1, 2, 6)]
# column into rownames
rownames(f2) <- f$ID
```

```{r}
f2 <- f[, -c(1, 2, 29)]
# column into rownames
rownames(f2) <- f$ID
# make into numeric matrix
f3 <- data.matrix(f2, rownames.force = NA)
f4 <- t(f3)

# same for df
# remove extra columns from df
df2 <- df[ , -c(3)]
# column into rownames
rownames(df2) <- df$ID
my_sample_col2 <- df2
my_sample_col3 <- as.data.frame(my_sample_col2)
rownames(my_sample_col3) <- df$ID
# lets add annotations of samples

# add annotations "Depth" and "soil_type" and change order
colnames(my_sample_col3) <- c("Treatment", "Depth")
my_sample_col3 <- my_sample_col3[, c(2,1)]

```



```{r}
# 1. Prepare group data

group <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_RA))
group <- subset(group, metabolism == "S_cycling")
rownames(group) <- group$gene  # Ensure gene names are row names
group <- group[match(rownames(f4), rownames(group)), ]  # Match order with f4

# Clean pathway names (no annotation needed)
group$pathway <- factor(group$pathway)  # Ensure it's a factor

# Order f4 rows by pathway (no gaps needed if no annotation)
f4_ordered <- f4[order(group$pathway), ]

row_gaps <- cumsum(table(group$pathway))[-length(table(group$pathway))]



#Create color palette
my_colour = list(
  "Treatment" = c(forest = "#1167b1", meadow = "#fbc02d", organic = "#8a8a8a", conventional =  "#b71c1c"),
  Depth = c('0-10 cm' = "#387212", '10-20 cm' = "#ADC476", '20-30 cm' = "#D8D2BA",'30-40 cm' = "#907852", '40-80 cm' = "#6A4C3A"))

# add gap between sample_types
gp_col = which(diff(as.numeric(factor(my_sample_col3$Treatment)))!=0)
```




```{r}
p2 <- as.ggplot(function() pheatmap(f4_ordered, cluster_cols = FALSE, cluster_rows = FALSE, annotation_col = my_sample_col3, annotation_colors = my_colour, gaps_col = gp_col, color=colorRampPalette(c("navy", "white", "red"))(50), show_colnames = FALSE, legend = TRUE, border_color = NA, cellheight = 16, fontsize = 14, fontsize_row = 14, annotation_names_row = FALSE, gaps_row = row_gaps, annotation_names_col = FALSE, scale = "row"))

p2
```

# METABOLIC LEVEL


Forest excluded due to too small replicate number!



```{r}
ps_x <- aggregate_rare(ps_RA, level = 'metabolism', detection = 0/100, prevalence = 0/140)
ps_x

# remove "Unknown"
ps_x <- subset_taxa(ps_x, metabolism!="Unknown")
ps_x

tax <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_x))

```


```{r}
#To remove those from your phyloseq object
ps_y <- subset_samples(ps_x, sample_type!="forest")
#This will return a ps object with the samples removed
ps_y

# You have only submitted samples, not OTUs. Define prevalence of each taxa
# (in how many samples did each taxa appear at least once)
prev0 = apply(X = otu_table(ps_y),
              MARGIN = ifelse(taxa_are_rows(ps_y), yes = 1, no = 2),
              FUN = function(x){sum(x > 0)})

# Execute prevalence filter, using `prune_taxa()` function
ps_y = prune_taxa((prev0 > 0), ps_y)
ps_y

```

# 2. GLMM 




```{r}
mx <- glmmTMB(Abundance ~ depth * treatment + (1|plot), 
              data = df2, 
              t_family(link = "logit"),
              dispformula = ~ depth,  # Variance varies by depth!
              control = glmmTMBControl(
                optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)
              ))

# 2. Check model diagnostics
summary(mx)
Anova(mx, type = "II", test = "Chisq")  # Type II tests

# 3. Validate residuals
sim_res <- simulateResiduals(mx, n = 250)
plot(sim_res)
testResiduals(sim_res)

# 1. Test if you need it:
mx0 <- glmmTMB(Abundance ~ depth * treatment + (1|plot), 
              data = df2, 
              t_family(link = "logit"),
              control = glmmTMBControl(
                optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)
              ))

# Likelihood ratio test
anova(mx0, mx)  # If p < 0.05, include dispformula
```


# 3. Final model: m1


```{r}
# 1. Fit model (with singular fit - this is fine!)
m1 <- glmmTMB(Abundance ~ depth * treatment + (1|plot), 
              data = df2, 
              t_family(link = "logit"),
              dispformula = ~ depth,  # Variance varies by depth!
              control = glmmTMBControl(
                optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)
              ))

# 2. Check model diagnostics
summary(m1)
Anova(m1, type = "II", test = "Chisq")  # Type II tests

##########################
logLik(m1)
##########################
# 1. Get predictions using ONLY the fixed effects (depth * treatment)
# re.form = NA drops the random effects from the prediction
fixed_preds <- predict(m1, type = "response", re.form = NA)

# 2. Get predictions using BOTH fixed and random effects
full_preds <- predict(m1, type = "response")

# 3. Get your actual raw response data from the model
raw_data <- m1$frame$Abundance

# 4. Compute manual R2 values
R2_marginal_manual    <- var(fixed_preds) / var(raw_data)
R2_conditional_manual <- var(full_preds) / var(raw_data)

# Print results
print(R2_marginal_manual)
print(R2_conditional_manual)

#########################

# 3. Validate residuals
sim_res <- simulateResiduals(m1, n = 250)
plot(sim_res)
testResiduals(sim_res)

# Extract full vcov as matrix - CORRECT WAY
vcov_obj <- vcov(m1)
vcov_full <- as.matrix(vcov_obj$cond)  # Use conditional part

# If you want the full vcov including dispersion parameters:
# Note: For t_family, this may not work, so we use conditional only
vcov_full <- as.matrix(vcov(m1)$cond)

# =========================================================================
# 1. INTERACTION POST-HOC 
# =========================================================================

# Option A: Comparing treatments within each specific depth
emm_inter_A <- emmeans(m1, ~ treatment | depth, 
                       type = "response",
                       vcov. = vcov_full)

cld_interaction_A <- as.data.frame(cld(emm_inter_A, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters, reversed = TRUE))
p_interaction_A <- as.data.frame(contrast(emm_inter_A, method = "pairwise", adjust = "tukey"))

# Option B: Comparing depths within each specific treatment
emm_inter_B <- emmeans(m1, ~ depth | treatment, 
                       type = "response",
                       vcov. = vcov_full)

cld_interaction_B <- as.data.frame(cld(emm_inter_B, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters, reversed = TRUE))
p_interaction_B <- as.data.frame(contrast(emm_inter_B, method = "pairwise", adjust = "tukey"))

# =========================================================================
# 2. DEPTH MAIN EFFECT POST-HOC 
# =========================================================================

emm_depth_main <- emmeans(m1, ~ depth, 
                          type = "response",
                          vcov. = vcov_full)

cld_depth_main <- as.data.frame(cld(emm_depth_main, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters, reversed = TRUE))
p_depth_main <- as.data.frame(contrast(emm_depth_main, method = "pairwise", adjust = "tukey"))

# =========================================================================
# 3. TREATMENT MAIN EFFECT POST-HOC 
# =========================================================================

emm_treatment_main <- emmeans(m1, ~ treatment, 
                              type = "response",
                              vcov. = vcov_full)

cld_treatment_main <- as.data.frame(cld(emm_treatment_main, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters, reversed = TRUE))
p_treatment_main <- as.data.frame(contrast(emm_treatment_main, method = "pairwise", adjust = "tukey"))

# =========================================================================
# 4. PRINT ALL OUTPUTS
# =========================================================================

print("--- Interaction: Treatment within Depth ---")
print(cld_interaction_A)
print(p_interaction_A)

print("--- Interaction: Depth within Treatment ---")
print(cld_interaction_B)
print(p_interaction_B)

print("--- Main Effect: Depth ---")
print(cld_depth_main)
print(p_depth_main)

print("--- Main Effect: Treatment ---")
print(cld_treatment_main)
print(p_treatment_main)
```

```{r}
# Get P-values:

# Get Letters:
```

# P VALUE CORRECTION!!

Collect P-Values from All Metabolism level Models

For each interaction and main effect, you should apply FDR correction separately because:

Interactions and main effects are testing different hypotheses

Treatment:Depth interaction tests are different from Depth:Treatment (they're the same interaction but presented differently)

Each main effect (depth and treatment) tests different things



```{r}

# ============================================
# LIST YOUR MODELS (metabolism level)
# ============================================

model_names <- c("m1", "m2", "m3", "m4")

# Create a list of models (only if they exist)
models <- list()
for (name in model_names) {
  if (exists(name)) {
    models[[name]] <- get(name)
  } else {
    warning(paste("Model", name, "not found"))
  }
}

# ============================================
# EXTRACT ALL RAW P-VALUES WITH GROUP INFO
# ============================================

all_raw_p <- c()
all_term_info <- c()
all_model_info <- c()
all_test_info <- c()
all_group_info <- c()  # NEW: Track which group each test belongs to

for (model_name in names(models)) {
  model <- models[[model_name]]
  
  # Get Anova table based on model type
  if (inherits(model, "glmmTMB")) {
    anova_table <- as.data.frame(car::Anova(model, type = "II", test = "Chisq"))
    raw_p <- anova_table[, "Pr(>Chisq)"]
    test_type <- "Chisq"
  } else if (inherits(model, "lmerMod")) {
    anova_table <- as.data.frame(car::Anova(model, type = "II", test = "F"))
    raw_p <- anova_table[, "Pr(>F)"]
    test_type <- "F"
  } else {
    warning(paste("Model", model_name, "not recognized"))
    next
  }
  
  terms <- rownames(anova_table)
  
  # Assign groups based on term type
  for (i in 1:length(terms)) {
    term <- terms[i]
    
    # Determine group
    if (grepl(":", term)) {
      # Interaction terms
      if (grepl("depth.*treatment|treatment.*depth", term)) {
        group <- "Interaction:Depth_Treatment"
      } else {
        group <- "Interaction:Other"
      }
    } else if (term == "depth") {
      group <- "Main:Depth"
    } else if (term == "treatment") {
      group <- "Main:Treatment"
    } else {
      group <- "Main:Other"
    }
    
    all_group_info <- c(all_group_info, group)
  }
  
  # Store all info
  all_raw_p <- c(all_raw_p, raw_p)
  all_term_info <- c(all_term_info, terms)
  all_model_info <- c(all_model_info, rep(model_name, length(raw_p)))
  all_test_info <- c(all_test_info, rep(test_type, length(raw_p)))
}

# ============================================
# APPLY FDR CORRECTION SEPARATELY BY GROUP
# ============================================

# Get unique groups
unique_groups <- unique(all_group_info)

# Initialize FDR p-values vector
fdr_p <- rep(NA, length(all_raw_p))

# Apply FDR separately to each group
for (group in unique_groups) {
  # Get indices for this group
  group_idx <- which(all_group_info == group)
  
  # Get p-values for this group
  group_p <- all_raw_p[group_idx]
  n_tests <- length(group_p)
  
  if (n_tests > 0) {
    # Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within this group
    sorted_idx <- order(group_p)
    sorted_p <- group_p[sorted_idx]
    fdr_values <- sorted_p * (n_tests / (1:n_tests))
    fdr_values <- pmin(fdr_values, 1)  # Cap at 1
    
    # Assign back to original order
    fdr_p[group_idx] <- fdr_values[order(sorted_idx)]
  }
}

# ============================================
# CREATE RESULTS TABLE
# ============================================

results <- data.frame(
  Model = all_model_info,
  Group = all_group_info,
  Term = all_term_info,
  Test = all_test_info,
  Raw_p = all_raw_p,
  FDR_p = fdr_p,
  Significant = ifelse(fdr_p < 0.05, "*", "")
)

# ============================================
# VIEW RESULTS
# ============================================

cat("========================================\n")
cat("FDR CORRECTION BY GROUP\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("Total models:", length(models), "\n")
cat("Total tests:", length(all_raw_p), "\n")

cat("\nTests by group:\n")
for (group in unique_groups) {
  n <- sum(all_group_info == group)
  sig <- sum(results$Significant[results$Group == group] == "*")
  cat("  ", group, ":", n, "tests,", sig, "significant\n")
}

cat("========================================\n\n")

print(results)

# ============================================
# SUMMARY BY GROUP
# ============================================

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("DETAILED SUMMARY BY GROUP\n")
cat("========================================\n")

for (group in unique_groups) {
  sub <- results[results$Group == group, ]
  cat("\n", "=== ", group, " ===\n", sep = "")
  cat("  Total tests:", nrow(sub), "\n")
  cat("  Significant (FDR < 0.05):", sum(sub$Significant == "*"), "\n")
  if (sum(sub$Significant == "*") > 0) {
    cat("  Significant terms:\n")
    for (i in 1:nrow(sub)) {
      if (sub$Significant[i] == "*") {
        cat("    -", sub$Term[i], "(raw p =", 
            format(sub$Raw_p[i], digits = 4), 
            ", FDR p =", format(sub$FDR_p[i], digits = 4), ")\n")
      }
    }
  }
  if (nrow(sub) > 0) {
    cat("  All terms:\n")
    for (i in 1:nrow(sub)) {
      cat("    -", sub$Term[i], ": raw =", 
          format(sub$Raw_p[i], digits = 4), 
          ", FDR =", format(sub$FDR_p[i], digits = 4), 
          sub$Significant[i], "\n")
    }
  }
}

# ============================================
# SUMMARY BY MODEL WITH GROUP BREAKDOWN
# ============================================

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("SUMMARY BY MODEL\n")
cat("========================================\n")

for (model_name in unique(results$Model)) {
  sub <- results[results$Model == model_name, ]
  cat("\n", model_name, ":\n", sep = "")
  cat("  Total terms:", nrow(sub), "\n")
  cat("  Significant:", sum(sub$Significant == "*"), "\n")
  
  # Breakdown by group within model
  for (group in unique(sub$Group)) {
    sub_group <- sub[sub$Group == group, ]
    cat("    ", group, ":", 
        sum(sub_group$Significant == "*"), "/", nrow(sub_group), 
        " significant\n", sep = "")
  }
  
  if (sum(sub$Significant == "*") > 0) {
    cat("  Significant terms:", 
        paste(sub$Term[sub$Significant == "*"], collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }
}

# ============================================
# OPTIONAL: EXPORT RESULTS BY GROUP
# ============================================

# Save full results
#write.csv(results, "FDR_results_by_group.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Save summary by group
summary_by_group <- data.frame(
  Group = unique_groups,
  Total_tests = sapply(unique_groups, function(g) sum(all_group_info == g)),
  Significant = sapply(unique_groups, function(g) sum(results$Significant[results$Group == g] == "*")),
  Sig_terms = sapply(unique_groups, function(g) {
    terms <- results$Term[results$Group == g & results$Significant == "*"]
    if (length(terms) > 0) paste(terms, collapse = "; ") else ""
  })
)
#write.csv(summary_by_group, "FDR_summary_by_group.csv", row.names = FALSE)


```

```{r}
                optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)
              ))
```

```{r}
full_preds <- predict(m5, type = "response")

raw_data <- m5$frame$Abundance

R2_conditional_manual <- var(full_preds) / var(raw_data)

print(R2_conditional_manual)
```

```{r}
  ggplot(aes(
```

```{r}
                optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)
              ))

              ))
```

```{r}
taxa <- "P_starv"

# Construct a data.frame with the selected
# taxonomic group and grouping
# relative
df2 <- filter(FG_df, OTU == taxa)
```



```{r}
Pstarv <- df2 %>%
  group_by(treatment, depth_numerical) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n())
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    y = mean,
    x = depth_numerical,
    color = treatment
  )) +
   geom_line(position = position_dodge(1.2)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, position = position_dodge(1.2)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
    width = 0.3,
    position = position_dodge(1.2),
    linetype = "solid",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = MyPalette) +
  labs(
    x = "Soil layer",
    y = "P starvation\nresponse regulation",
    color = "Treatment"
  ) +
  theme_cowplot() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),  # Bold axis titles only
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),  # No bold for legend text
    legend.title = element_blank(),  # Remove legend title (alternative method)
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5)
  ) +
  scale_x_reverse(
    breaks = c(60, 35, 25, 15, 5),
    labels = c("40-80 cm", "30-40 cm", "20-30 cm", "10-20 cm", "0-10 cm")
  ) + theme(legend.title=element_blank())

print(Pstarv)
```

Combined: denitrification

```{r}
# Extract the "denitrify" data
denitrify_data <- filter(FG_df, OTU == "denitrify")

# Combine/sum the abundances by treatment and depth
combined_data <- denitrify_data %>%
  left_join(
    filter(FG_df, OTU == "denitrify_DNRA") %>%
      rename(Abundance_DNRA = Abundance),
    by = c("treatment", "depth_numerical", "depth", "Sample")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Abundance_combined = Abundance + Abundance_DNRA
  )

# Now create the figure with the summed values
denitrify <- combined_data %>%
  group_by(treatment, depth_numerical) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(Abundance_combined, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd(Abundance_combined, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n())
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    y = mean,
    x = depth_numerical,
    color = treatment
  )) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(1.2)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, position = position_dodge(1.2)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
    width = 0.3,
    position = position_dodge(1.2),
    linetype = "solid",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
 # Set abundance axis labels BEFORE coord_flip (using scale_y_continuous)
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 4)
  ) +
  # Set depth axis labels (using scale_x_reverse for depth)
  scale_x_reverse(
    breaks = c(60, 35, 25, 15, 5),
    labels = c("40-80 cm", "30-40 cm", "20-30 cm", "10-20 cm", "0-10 cm")
  ) +
  coord_flip() +  # Now flip AFTER setting both axes
  scale_colour_manual(values = MyPalette) +
  labs(
    x = "Soil layer",
    y = "Denitrification",
    color = "Treatment"
  ) +
  theme_cowplot() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5)
  )

print(denitrify)
```

```{r}
    Abundance_combined = Abundance + Abundance_DNRA
  )

# Now create the figure with the summed values
DNRA2 <- combined_data %>%
  group_by(treatment, depth_numerical) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(Abundance_combined, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd(Abundance_combined, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n())
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    y = mean,
    x = depth_numerical,
    color = treatment
  )) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(1.2)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, position = position_dodge(1.2)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
    width = 0.3,
    position = position_dodge(1.2),
    linetype = "solid",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = MyPalette) +
  labs(
    x = "Soil layer",
    y = "DNRA",
    color = "Treatment"
  ) +
  theme_cowplot() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5)
  ) +
  scale_x_reverse(
    breaks = c(60, 35, 25, 15, 5),
    labels = c("40-80 cm", "30-40 cm", "20-30 cm", "10-20 cm", "0-10 cm")
  )

print(DNRA2)
```

Forest excluded due to too small replicate number!

```{r}
#To remove those from your phyloseq object
ps_y <- subset_samples(ps_RA_phyla_aggr_good, sample_type!="forest")
#This will return a ps object with the samples removed
ps_y

# You have only submitted samples, not OTUs. Define prevalence of each taxa
# (in how many samples did each taxa appear at least once)
prev0 = apply(X = otu_table(ps_y),
              MARGIN = ifelse(taxa_are_rows(ps_y), yes = 1, no = 2),
              FUN = function(x){sum(x > 0)})

# Execute prevalence filter, using `prune_taxa()` function
ps_y = prune_taxa((prev0 > 0), ps_y)
ps_y

```

# 2. GLMM 



```{r}
mx <- glmmTMB(Abundance ~ depth * treatment, 
              data = df2, 
              ordbeta(link = "logit"),
              control = glmmTMBControl(
                optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)
              ))

# 2. Check model diagnostics
summary(mx)
Anova(mx, type = "II", test = "Chisq")  # Type II tests

# 3. Validate residuals
```

```{r}
x <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_x))

tax_table(ps_x) <- tax_table(x)
```



```{r}
ps_RA_phyla_aggr_good <- microbiome::aggregate_rare(ps_x, level = 'pathway', detection = 0/140, prevalence = 0/140)
ps_RA_phyla_aggr_good
```


Forest excluded due to too small replicate number!

```{r}
#To remove those from your phyloseq object
ps_y <- subset_samples(ps_RA_phyla_aggr_good, sample_type!="forest")
#This will return a ps object with the samples removed
ps_y

# You have only submitted samples, not OTUs. Define prevalence of each taxa
# (in how many samples did each taxa appear at least once)
prev0 = apply(X = otu_table(ps_y),
              MARGIN = ifelse(taxa_are_rows(ps_y), yes = 1, no = 2),
              FUN = function(x){sum(x > 0)})

# Execute prevalence filter, using `prune_taxa()` function
ps_y = prune_taxa((prev0 > 0), ps_y)
ps_y

```

# 2. GLMM 




```{r}
mx <- glmmTMB(Abundance ~ depth * treatment + (1|plot), 
              data = df2, 
              t_family(link = "logit"),
              dispformula = ~ depth,  # Variance varies by depth!
              control = glmmTMBControl(
                optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)
              ))

# 2. Check model diagnostics
summary(mx)
Anova(mx, type = "II", test = "Chisq")  # Type II tests

# 3. Validate residuals
sim_res <- simulateResiduals(mx, n = 250)
plot(sim_res)
testResiduals(sim_res)

# 1. Test if you need it:
mx0 <- glmmTMB(Abundance ~ depth * treatment + (1|plot), 
              data = df2, 
              t_family(link = "logit"),
              control = glmmTMBControl(
                optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)
              ))

# Likelihood ratio test
anova(mx0, mx)  # If p < 0.05, include dispformula
```






# 3. Final model: m13


```{r}
# 1. Fit model (with singular fit - this is fine!)
m13 <- glmmTMB(Abundance ~ depth * treatment + (1|plot), 
              data = df2, 
              t_family(link = "logit"),
              control = glmmTMBControl(
                optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)
              ))

# 2. Check model diagnostics
summary(m13)
Anova(m13, type = "II", test = "Chisq")  # Type II tests

##########################

##########################
# 1. Get predictions using ONLY the fixed effects (depth * treatment)
# re.form = NA drops the random effects from the prediction
fixed_preds <- predict(m13, type = "response", re.form = NA)

# 2. Get predictions using BOTH fixed and random effects
full_preds <- predict(m13, type = "response")

# 3. Get your actual raw response data from the model
raw_data <- m13$frame$Abundance

# 4. Compute manual R2 values
R2_marginal_manual    <- var(fixed_preds) / var(raw_data)
R2_conditional_manual <- var(full_preds) / var(raw_data)

# Print results
print(R2_marginal_manual)
print(R2_conditional_manual)

#########################

# 3. Validate residuals
sim_res <- simulateResiduals(m13, n = 250)
plot(sim_res)
testResiduals(sim_res)
```

```{r}
levels(FG_df$OTU)
```

```{r}
taxa <- "nitrify"

# Construct a data.frame with the selected
# taxonomic group and grouping
# relative
df2 <- filter(FG_df, OTU == taxa)
```




# 1. Data distribution

```{r}
# Basic density plot in ggplot2
ggplot(df2, aes(x = Abundance)) +
  geom_density()
```




```{r}
shapiro.test(df2$Abundance)
```




--> ~ heavy-tailed gamma distribution



```{r}
fig <- df2 %>%
  group_by(treatment, depth_numerical) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(n())
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    y = mean,
    x = depth_numerical,
    color = treatment
  )) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(1.2)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, position = position_dodge(1.2)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
    width = 0.3,
    position = position_dodge(1.2),
    linetype = "solid",
    alpha = 0.5
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_x_reverse() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = MyPalette) +
  labs(
    x = "Soil layer",
    y = "Proportion",
    color = "Treatment"
  ) +
  theme_cowplot() +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 18),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 22, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 22),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 22),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 22, hjust = 0.5),
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, size = 0.5),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 22, face = "bold")
  ) +
  scale_x_reverse(
    breaks = c(60, 35, 25, 15, 5),
    labels = c("40-80 cm", "30-40 cm", "20-30 cm", "10-20 cm", "0-10 cm")
  ) + theme(legend.title=element_blank())

print(fig)
```



# 2. GLMM 




```{r}
mx <- glmmTMB(Abundance ~ depth * treatment + (1|plot), 
              data = df2, 
              t_family(link = "logit"),
              dispformula = ~ depth,  # Variance varies by depth!
              control = glmmTMBControl(
                optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)
              ))

# 2. Check model diagnostics
summary(mx)
Anova(mx, type = "II", test = "Chisq")  # Type II tests

# 3. Validate residuals
sim_res <- simulateResiduals(mx, n = 250)
plot(sim_res)
testResiduals(sim_res)

# 1. Test if you need it:
mx0 <- glmmTMB(Abundance ~ depth * treatment + (1|plot), 
              data = df2, 
              t_family(link = "logit"),
              control = glmmTMBControl(
                optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)
              ))

# Likelihood ratio test
anova(mx0, mx)  # If p < 0.05, include dispformula
```




# 3. Final model: m16


```{r}
# 1. Fit model (with singular fit - this is fine!)
m16 <- glmmTMB(Abundance ~ depth * treatment + (1|plot), 
              data = df2, 
              t_family(link = "logit"),
              control = glmmTMBControl(
                optCtrl = list(iter.max = 1000, eval.max = 1000)
              ))

# 2. Check model diagnostics
summary(m16)
Anova(m16, type = "II", test = "Chisq")  # Type II tests

##########################

##########################
# 1. Get predictions using ONLY the fixed effects (depth * treatment)
# re.form = NA drops the random effects from the prediction
fixed_preds <- predict(m16, type = "response", re.form = NA)

# 2. Get predictions using BOTH fixed and random effects
full_preds <- predict(m16, type = "response")

# 3. Get your actual raw response data from the model
raw_data <- m16$frame$Abundance

# 4. Compute manual R2 values
R2_marginal_manual    <- var(fixed_preds) / var(raw_data)
R2_conditional_manual <- var(full_preds) / var(raw_data)

# Print results
print(R2_marginal_manual)
print(R2_conditional_manual)

#########################

# 3. Validate residuals
sim_res <- simulateResiduals(m16, n = 250)
plot(sim_res)
testResiduals(sim_res)


##########################

# Force emmeans to always calculate back-transformed real-scale proportions (0 to 1)
# while performing pairwise tests safely on the internal logit scale.

library(emmeans)
library(multcomp)

# =========================================================================
# 1. INTERACTION POST-HOC 
# =========================================================================

# Option A: Comparing treatments within each specific depth
emm_inter_A <- emmeans(m16, ~ treatment | depth, type = "response")
# Get Letters:
cld_interaction_A <- as.data.frame(cld(emm_inter_A, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters, reversed = TRUE))
# Get P-values:
p_interaction_A <- as.data.frame(contrast(emm_inter_A, method = "pairwise", adjust = "tukey"))


# Option B: Comparing depths within each specific treatment
emm_inter_B <- emmeans(m16, ~ depth | treatment, type = "response")
# Get Letters:
cld_interaction_B <- as.data.frame(cld(emm_inter_B, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters, reversed = TRUE))
# Get P-values:
p_interaction_B <- as.data.frame(contrast(emm_inter_B, method = "pairwise", adjust = "tukey"))


# =========================================================================
# 2. DEPTH MAIN EFFECT POST-HOC 
# =========================================================================

emm_depth_main <- emmeans(m16, ~ depth, type = "response")
# Get Letters:
cld_depth_main <- as.data.frame(cld(emm_depth_main, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters, reversed = TRUE))
# Get P-values:
p_depth_main <- as.data.frame(contrast(emm_depth_main, method = "pairwise", adjust = "tukey"))


# =========================================================================
# 3. TREATMENT MAIN EFFECT POST-HOC 
# =========================================================================

emm_treatment_main <- emmeans(m16, ~ treatment, type = "response")
# Get Letters:
cld_treatment_main <- as.data.frame(cld(emm_treatment_main, adjust = "tukey", Letters = letters, reversed = TRUE))
# Get P-values:
p_treatment_main <- as.data.frame(contrast(emm_treatment_main, method = "pairwise", adjust = "tukey"))


# =========================================================================
# 4. Print all outputs to your console
# =========================================================================
print("--- Interaction: Treatment within Depth (LETTERS & P-VALUES) ---")
print(cld_interaction_A)
print(p_interaction_A)

print("--- Interaction: Depth within Treatment (LETTERS & P-VALUES) ---")
print(cld_interaction_B)
print(p_interaction_B)

print("--- Main Effect: Depth (LETTERS & P-VALUES) ---")
print(cld_depth_main)
print(p_depth_main)

print("--- Main Effect: Treatment (LETTERS & P-VALUES) ---")
print(cld_treatment_main)
print(p_treatment_main)


```










# S-cycling




```{r}
ps_x <- subset_taxa(ps_RA, metabolism=="S_cycling")
ps_x
```


```{r}
x <- as.data.frame(tax_table(ps_x))
x <- x[, c(1,5,6,2:4)]
x <- as.matrix(x)
tax_table(ps_x) <- tax_table(x)
```



```{r}
ps_RA_phyla_aggr_good <- microbiome::aggregate_rare(ps_x, level = 'pathway', detection = 0/140, prevalence = 0/140)
ps_RA_phyla_aggr_good
```



Forest excluded due to too small replicate number!


```{r}
#To remove those from your phyloseq object
ps_y <- subset_samples(ps_RA_phyla_aggr_good, sample_type!="forest")
#This will return a ps object with the samples removed
ps_y

# You have only submitted samples, not OTUs. Define prevalence of each taxa
# (in how many samples did each taxa appear at least once)
prev0 = apply(X = otu_table(ps_y),
              MARGIN = ifelse(taxa_are_rows(ps_y), yes = 1, no = 2),
              FUN = function(x){sum(x > 0)})

# Execute prevalence filter, using `prune_taxa()` function
ps_y = prune_taxa((prev0 > 0), ps_y)
ps_y

```




```{r}
#create data table
FG_df <-  psmelt(ps_y)

FG_df$treatment <- factor(FG_df$sample_type, 
                            levels = c("meadow", "organic", "conventional"))

levels(FG_df$treatment)

FG_df$depth <- factor(FG_df$depth, 
                            levels = c("0...10", "10...20", "20...30", "30...40", "40..."))

levels(FG_df$depth)

FG_df$OTU <- as.factor(FG_df$OTU)


```





# 1. ASR



```{r}
levels(FG_df$OTU)
```


```{r}
# Extract and aggregate denitrify data
denitrify_data <- FG_df %>%
  filter(OTU == "ASR") %>%
  group_by(treatment, depth_numerical, depth, plot, Sample) %>%
  summarise(Abundance_denitrify = sum(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Extract and aggregate DNRA data
dnra_data <- FG_df %>%
  filter(OTU == "DSR_ASR") %>%
  group_by(treatment, depth_numerical, depth, plot, Sample) %>%
  summarise(Abundance_DNRA = sum(Abundance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Join the aggregated data
df2 <- denitrify_data %>%
  left_join(dnra_data, by = c("treatment", "depth_numerical", "depth", "plot", "Sample")) %>%
  mutate(
    Abundance = Abundance_denitrify + Abundance_DNRA
  )
```

# P VALUE CORRECTION!!

Collect P-Values from All Metabolism level Models

For each interaction and main effect, you should apply FDR correction separately because:

Interactions and main effects are testing different hypotheses

Treatment:Depth interaction tests are different from Depth:Treatment (they're the same interaction but presented differently)

Each main effect (depth and treatment) tests different things



```{r}

# ============================================
# LIST YOUR MODELS (metabolism level)
# ============================================

# Create model names from m5 to m21
model_names <- paste0("m", 5:21)

# Create a list of models (only if they exist)
models <- list()
for (name in model_names) {
  if (exists(name)) {
    models[[name]] <- get(name)
  } else {
    warning(paste("Model", name, "not found"))
  }
}

# ============================================
# EXTRACT ALL RAW P-VALUES WITH GROUP INFO
# ============================================

all_raw_p <- c()
all_term_info <- c()
all_model_info <- c()
all_test_info <- c()
all_group_info <- c()  # NEW: Track which group each test belongs to

for (model_name in names(models)) {
  model <- models[[model_name]]
  
  # Get Anova table based on model type
  if (inherits(model, "glmmTMB")) {
    anova_table <- as.data.frame(car::Anova(model, type = "II", test = "Chisq"))
    raw_p <- anova_table[, "Pr(>Chisq)"]
    test_type <- "Chisq"
  } else if (inherits(model, "lmerMod")) {
    anova_table <- as.data.frame(car::Anova(model, type = "II", test = "F"))
    raw_p <- anova_table[, "Pr(>F)"]
    test_type <- "F"
  } else {
    warning(paste("Model", model_name, "not recognized"))
    next
  }
  
  terms <- rownames(anova_table)
  
  # Assign groups based on term type
  for (i in 1:length(terms)) {
    term <- terms[i]
    
    # Determine group
    if (grepl(":", term)) {
      # Interaction terms
      if (grepl("depth.*treatment|treatment.*depth", term)) {
        group <- "Interaction:Depth_Treatment"
      } else {
        group <- "Interaction:Other"
      }
    } else if (term == "depth") {
      group <- "Main:Depth"
    } else if (term == "treatment") {
      group <- "Main:Treatment"
    } else {
      group <- "Main:Other"
    }
    
    all_group_info <- c(all_group_info, group)
  }
  
  # Store all info
  all_raw_p <- c(all_raw_p, raw_p)
  all_term_info <- c(all_term_info, terms)
  all_model_info <- c(all_model_info, rep(model_name, length(raw_p)))
  all_test_info <- c(all_test_info, rep(test_type, length(raw_p)))
}

# ============================================
# APPLY FDR CORRECTION SEPARATELY BY GROUP
# ============================================

# Get unique groups
unique_groups <- unique(all_group_info)

# Initialize FDR p-values vector
fdr_p <- rep(NA, length(all_raw_p))

# Apply FDR separately to each group
for (group in unique_groups) {
  # Get indices for this group
  group_idx <- which(all_group_info == group)
  
  # Get p-values for this group
  group_p <- all_raw_p[group_idx]
  n_tests <- length(group_p)
  
  if (n_tests > 0) {
    # Benjamini-Hochberg FDR within this group
    sorted_idx <- order(group_p)
    sorted_p <- group_p[sorted_idx]
    fdr_values <- sorted_p * (n_tests / (1:n_tests))
    fdr_values <- pmin(fdr_values, 1)  # Cap at 1
    
    # Assign back to original order
    fdr_p[group_idx] <- fdr_values[order(sorted_idx)]
  }
}

# ============================================
# CREATE RESULTS TABLE
# ============================================

results <- data.frame(
  Model = all_model_info,
  Group = all_group_info,
  Term = all_term_info,
  Test = all_test_info,
  Raw_p = all_raw_p,
  FDR_p = fdr_p,
  Significant = ifelse(fdr_p < 0.05, "*", "")
)

# ============================================
# VIEW RESULTS
# ============================================

cat("========================================\n")
cat("FDR CORRECTION BY GROUP\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("Total models:", length(models), "\n")
cat("Total tests:", length(all_raw_p), "\n")

cat("\nTests by group:\n")
for (group in unique_groups) {
  n <- sum(all_group_info == group)
  sig <- sum(results$Significant[results$Group == group] == "*")
  cat("  ", group, ":", n, "tests,", sig, "significant\n")
}

cat("========================================\n\n")

print(results)

# ============================================
# SUMMARY BY GROUP
# ============================================

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("DETAILED SUMMARY BY GROUP\n")
cat("========================================\n")

for (group in unique_groups) {
  sub <- results[results$Group == group, ]
  cat("\n", "=== ", group, " ===\n", sep = "")
  cat("  Total tests:", nrow(sub), "\n")
  cat("  Significant (FDR < 0.05):", sum(sub$Significant == "*"), "\n")
  if (sum(sub$Significant == "*") > 0) {
    cat("  Significant terms:\n")
    for (i in 1:nrow(sub)) {
      if (sub$Significant[i] == "*") {
        cat("    -", sub$Term[i], "(raw p =", 
            format(sub$Raw_p[i], digits = 4), 
            ", FDR p =", format(sub$FDR_p[i], digits = 4), ")\n")
      }
    }
  }
  if (nrow(sub) > 0) {
    cat("  All terms:\n")
    for (i in 1:nrow(sub)) {
      cat("    -", sub$Term[i], ": raw =", 
          format(sub$Raw_p[i], digits = 4), 
          ", FDR =", format(sub$FDR_p[i], digits = 4), 
          sub$Significant[i], "\n")
    }
  }
}

# ============================================
# SUMMARY BY MODEL WITH GROUP BREAKDOWN
# ============================================

cat("\n========================================\n")
cat("SUMMARY BY MODEL\n")
cat("========================================\n")

for (model_name in unique(results$Model)) {
  sub <- results[results$Model == model_name, ]
  cat("\n", model_name, ":\n", sep = "")
  cat("  Total terms:", nrow(sub), "\n")
  cat("  Significant:", sum(sub$Significant == "*"), "\n")
  
  # Breakdown by group within model
  for (group in unique(sub$Group)) {
    sub_group <- sub[sub$Group == group, ]
    cat("    ", group, ":", 
        sum(sub_group$Significant == "*"), "/", nrow(sub_group), 
        " significant\n", sep = "")
  }
  
  if (sum(sub$Significant == "*") > 0) {
    cat("  Significant terms:", 
        paste(sub$Term[sub$Significant == "*"], collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }
}

# ============================================
# OPTIONAL: EXPORT RESULTS BY GROUP
# ============================================

# Save full results
#write.csv(results, "FDR_results_by_group.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Save summary by group
summary_by_group <- data.frame(
  Group = unique_groups,
  Total_tests = sapply(unique_groups, function(g) sum(all_group_info == g)),
  Significant = sapply(unique_groups, function(g) sum(results$Significant[results$Group == g] == "*")),
  Sig_terms = sapply(unique_groups, function(g) {
    terms <- results$Term[results$Group == g & results$Significant == "*"]
    if (length(terms) > 0) paste(terms, collapse = "; ") else ""
  })
)
```
